country_context.note: This profile focuses on Putonghua in mainland China. Mandarin varieties outside mainland China and regional Sinitic languages require separate context profiles.

coverage_targets: standard pronunciation reference and its relation to Beijing speech
regional Mandarin accents such as Northeastern, Southwestern, and Jianghuai varieties
four lexical tones and neutral tone
retroflex initials, erhua, tone sandhi, and connected-speech changes
forms of address and kinship terms
politeness, indirect requests, refusal, and face-related interaction
sentence-final particles and discourse markers
regional and generational variation
Putonghua pronunciation and grammar standards
simplified Chinese characters in mainland standard writing
pinyin conventions
formal, academic, public-service, and everyday written registers
colloquial reductions and discourse particles
internet slang, abbreviations, and memes with date labels
regional vocabulary kept distinct from standard Putonghua
character-based wordplay and homophones with cultural context
common insults and profanity
literal meaning versus pragmatic force
severity, target, and situational appropriateness
regional differences and neutral Indonesian explanations
Yue/Cantonese, Wu, Min, Hakka, Xiang, Gan, Jin, and other Sinitic varieties
Tibetan, Uyghur, Mongolian, Zhuang, Kazakh, Korean, and other minority languages
Do not treat mutually unintelligible varieties as interchangeable accents of Putonghua

sources.title: PRC Ministry of Education: Overview of Chinese Language and Writing Systems
Center for Applied Linguistics: The Chinese Language and Language Planning in China

verification.notes: Profile framework created. Lexical examples, slang, and profanity entries require dictionary and native-speaker review.
